title: render() always throws: `save` and `report` are never defined or imported, so the catch handler itself throws
evidence: app.js has no import, no declaration and no export of `save` or `report` (whole file read, 8 lines). notes.js, the only other file, does not define them either; the change map reports no other file refers to these files. Traced: line 6 calls undefined `save` -> ReferenceError -> the catch calls undefined `report` -> a second ReferenceError that nothing catches. Line 5 has the same flaw for corrupt JSON. I could not execute it (Bash was denied), so this is traced, not run.
failing_case: Call render(el, 'x') with an empty localStorage. Line 3 sets textContent, line 5 parses null (fine), line 6 throws ReferenceError: save is not defined, the catch calls report(e), which throws ReferenceError: report is not defined. render() never returns `data`; the caller gets an exception on every call. With corrupt JSON in the 'cart' key, line 5 fails the same way.
remediation: Import or define `save` and `report` in the module (or pass them in), and add a test that calls render() with empty, corrupt and valid cart data. Keep the handler from being able to throw, for example by reporting through console.error.
